source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: Treats reasoning as planning in an MDP: the same LLM is both world model (predicts next state) and policy; MCTS searches with reward = self-evaluation x state confidence.
numbers: Blocksworld, LLaMA-33B: CoT solves only a few 2-step cases; RAP averages 64% success over problems up to 6 steps (42% on 6-step within 20 iterations); beats GPT-4 CoT by 33% relative. GSM8k: CoT 29.4, CoT+SC(10) 46.8, RAP(1) 48.6, RAP(10) 51.6 (aggregation ~3 points more). ProntoQA: prediction 94.2 vs CoT 87.8, proof accuracy 78.8 vs 64.8.
quote: maintaining the world state during reasoning, RAP can recognize valid actions for the current state
limits: States and rewards are LLM-judged (noisy); 20 MCTS iterations cost far more tokens than one CoT; the self-evaluation reward lost accuracy with more iterations in an ablation.
agent_relevance: Closest published instance of an MDP formalism inside an LLM loop. Counted search over states with a real state description beats free chain of thought. Reward from the model's own judgment is the weak part (matches our G2).

source: Zhao, Lee & Hsu (2023) Large Language Models as Commonsense Knowledge for Large-Scale Task Planning (LLM-MCTS)
finding: LLM supplies a commonsense prior belief over the hidden world (world model) and a policy heuristic inside MCTS for a partially observable household task; plain UCT fails.
numbers: VirtualHome success %, seen tasks: Simple GPT3.5-MCTS 91.4 vs GPT3.5 policy 83.4 vs fine-tuned GPT2 81.3; Compositional 71.2 vs 47.0 vs 59.0. Unseen: Simple 82.9 vs 74.3 vs 65.5; Compositional 71.9 vs 43.3 vs 39.9. UCT alone 0.0 in every column. (Table was column-garbled in PDF extraction; row assignment is my best reading.)
limits: Simulated household environment, GPT-3.5 era, 30-step cap. Hardest novel compositional tasks stay low for all methods.
agent_relevance: Belief over hidden state from an LLM prior plus search is a working POMDP-style recipe. Gain is largest on novel and compositional tasks, where a single-shot policy is weakest. The paper also proposes a description-length rule: use the LLM as world model when the model is shorter to describe than the policy.

source: Feng et al. (2023) Alphazero-like Tree-Search can Guide LLM Decoding and Training (TS-LLM)
finding: Only the arXiv title was seen: learned value function plus tree search guides LLM decoding and training, AlphaZero style.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened beyond the title.
agent_relevance: Value-guided search is the MDP solution method that RAP and ToT approximate without a learned value.

source: Krishnamurthy, Harris, Foster, Zhang & Slivkins (2024) Can large language models explore in-context?
finding: GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama2 as bandit agents with the history in the prompt, 32 prompt designs per model. Only one setup explored well: GPT-4 + hint to explore + externally summarised per-arm averages (sufficient statistics) + zero-shot chain of thought.
numbers: Basic GPT-4 prompt had suffix failures (never pulls the best arm again after early rounds) in over 60% of replicates at T=500. Other failure: near-uniform arm choice. Only 1 configuration succeeded. The same setup without the summary failed.
quote: only one configuration resulted in satisfactory exploratory behavior
limits: Simple multi-armed bandits only; summarising history externally may be impossible in complex settings where the belief is not a few numbers. Authors suggest fine-tuning may be needed.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence that the program, not the model, should maintain the sufficient statistic (belief state) and hand it over each step. Fits our rule that code counts and the model fills a slot.

source: Nie et al. (2024/2025) EVOLvE: Evaluating and Optimizing LLMs For In-Context Exploration
finding: Benchmarks LLMs on context-free and contextual bandits and tests injecting algorithm knowledge: algorithm-guided support at inference (summarised history plus UCB-style hints) and algorithm distillation by demonstration or fine-tuning.
numbers: Summarised history gave 50.2% overall win-rate versus 27.5% for raw history in one comparison. Smaller models trained on UCB traces beat larger models on several tasks (abstract: surpass larger models; text: beats Gemini-1.5 Pro in places).
limits: Bandits are stateless (no transitions), so only the belief-update half of POMDP control is tested. Win-rates are relative to a pool of baselines.
agent_relevance: Second independent source that a summarised sufficient statistic beats raw history, and that handing the model an explicit algorithm step helps. Backs a program-held belief state.

source: Lee et al. (2023) Supervised Pretraining Can Learn In-Context Reinforcement Learning (Decision-Pretrained Transformer)
finding: A transformer trained to predict the optimal action from an in-context dataset of interactions behaves like posterior (Thompson) sampling and explores online without being trained to.
numbers: Theory: DPT is an efficient implementation of Bayesian posterior sampling, with regret guarantees. Empirically solves bandits and MDPs in-context, explores online, is conservative offline.
quote: exhibiting both exploration online and conservatism offline
limits: Needs pretraining on a task distribution with optimal-action labels; small transformers, not general LLMs. I read the abstract and introduction, not every experiment.
agent_relevance: Shows in-context belief updating is learnable, so off-the-shelf failures are about training, not impossibility. Prompt-only scaffolds must supply what training did not.

source: Shai et al. (2024/2025) Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
finding: Transformers trained on next-token prediction of hidden Markov processes linearly encode the Bayesian belief state over hidden states, including fractal geometry (Mess3, a 3-state HMM). Belief information reaches beyond the next token.
numbers: Linear regression from the residual stream onto the predicted belief simplex recovers the fractal shape; error falls during training; shuffling controls remove the fit. (Exact MSE values not extracted.)
limits: Toy synthetic HMMs and small transformers, not natural-language models.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a sequence model can carry a POMDP belief internally. Does not show a chat LLM does so reliably in context; see the Bayesian-teaching line.

source: Li et al. (2023) Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task (Othello-GPT)
finding: A GPT trained only on legal Othello move sequences forms an internal board state; interventions on it change move predictions.
numbers: Illegal-move error 0.01% (synthetic-trained) vs 93.29% untrained. Linear probe error never below 20%; 2-layer nonlinear probe error falls to 1.7% at best layer (synthetic data), 9.4% (championship data), vs about 25.5% on a random network.
limits: Board is fully observable from the move list (state tracking, not hidden-state belief). Later work found a linear structure under a different encoding, which this paper did not test.
agent_relevance: Supports the claim that sequence models track state when the state is a function of the history, an MDP-like tracking skill.

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen & van Steenkiste (2025/2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Off-the-shelf LLMs update beliefs about a hidden user preference poorly over 5 rounds of flight recommendations; most plateau after round 1. Fine-tuning on a Bayesian assistant's outputs fixes much of it and transfers to hotels and real web shopping.
numbers: 624 simulated users, 5 rounds, 100 held-out flight sets per eval. Models: Gemma2 9B/27B, Llama3 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 7B/32B, GPT-4.1 Mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro, plus 48 humans. All below the Bayesian Assistant (about 68% final accuracy, read from figure labels). Small models: original about 37, oracle teaching about 48 to 57, Bayesian teaching about 53 to 62 (approximate, from figure labels). Bayesian beat oracle teaching for all three; p<0.001.
quote: LLMs' performance often plateaus after a single interaction, pointing to a limited ability to adapt to new information
limits: Needs fine-tuning, so not a prompt-only fix; follow-up prompt experiments gave no meaningful improvement. Simulated users with a few preference features.
agent_relevance: Direct test of POMDP belief updating in LLMs: models do not update like a Bayes filter, and humans improve more than most LLMs. Argues for computing the posterior in code and showing it, not relying on the model to do the update.

source: Li, Tamkin, Goodman & Andreas (2023) Eliciting Human Preferences with Language Models (GATE)
finding: LMs ask the user open-ended questions or generate edge cases to infer task intent (email validation, content recommendation, moral reasoning). Pre-registered user studies.
numbers: Elicitation often gave more informative responses than user-written prompts or labels; significant at 0.05 in all domain comparisons but one; users reported less effort. Final accuracy extended to the 5-minute mark for fair comparison.
limits: Plain LM questioner, no explicit belief or information-gain computation; I did not extract per-domain effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Informal baseline for 'ask to reduce uncertainty'. Later work (OPEN, UoT) adds an explicit belief and information gain.

source: Handa et al. (2024) Bayesian Preference Elicitation with Language Models (OPEN)
finding: Combines Bayesian optimal experimental design (expected information gain over a feature belief) with an LM that verbalises the query.
numbers: User study, Time-Integrated Delta Accuracy (TIDA). OPEN beat LM-only pairwise questioning and BOED-only without verbalisation. Open-ended LM questions scored higher under LM prediction, but OPEN's tracked-belief prediction outweighed it. Numeric TIDA values were in a figure I did not read out.
limits: Content-recommendation domain; small user study; no numeric TIDA extracted.
agent_relevance: The POMDP loop done properly: explicit belief, choose the query by expected information gain, the LM only talks. Matches our split of roles.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking in LLMs (UoT)
finding: Simulates future question and answer branches, scores each question by expected information gain over remaining hypotheses, propagates reward through the tree, picks the best question. A belief-state lookahead built around the LLM.
numbers: Averaged over 5 datasets and 5 LLMs, success rate +38.1% over direct prompting; Llama3-70B +46.6%; beats CoT-SC by 33.8%, Reflexion by 29.9%, adapted ToT by 12.4%. GPT-4 medical DX 97.0% success; troubleshooting 43.7 -> 67.3%. Llama3-70B closed-set DX 83.7 -> 90.4, MedDG 60.2 -> 64.3. Simulation depth limited to 3 for cost.
limits: The answerer is itself GPT-4 simulating the environment (checked on 10% of logs); the medical task is simplified; uniform prior over hypotheses.
agent_relevance: Best published case for an information-gain question selector inside an LLM loop. Gains are largest where the model's own question choice is poor. Fits an operator that asks the most splitting question.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
finding: Argues autoregressive LLMs cannot plan or self-verify alone; proposes that the LLM generates, external sound critics verify, and results are back-prompted.
numbers: Autonomous mode: only about 12% of GPT-4 plans executable and goal-reaching on PlanBench. Mystery Blocksworld one-shot: GPT-4o 28.3%, Claude-3-Opus 48.2%, Gemini Pro 11.3%. With VAL back-prompting up to 15 rounds, Blocksworld reaches 82% and Logistics 70%; Mystery BW only about 10%.
quote: a system that takes constant time to produce the next token cannot possibly be doing principled reasoning on its own
limits: Position paper; numbers re-reported from Valmeekam et al. 2023; newer reasoning models post-date the tables.
agent_relevance: Strong support for G2 and G3: the model proposes, a sound checker disposes. Also a warning that verifier loops fail when the model cannot propose plausible candidates.

source: Valmeekam, Marquez & Kambhampati (2023) Can LLMs Really Improve by Self-critiquing Their Own Plans?
finding: GPT-4 as both planner and verifier on Blocksworld: self-critique does not help much, an external sound verifier does.
numbers: 100 instances: generator alone 40%; LLM+LLM with back-prompting 55%; LLM+VAL (sound verifier) with back-prompting 88%. LLM verifier correct on 61/100 instances. Feedback detail (n=50): binary only 74%, plus first error 86%, plus all errors 86%.
limits: One domain, one model. Abstract says self-critiquing appears to diminish plan generation; the 55% vs 40% in the table is the back-prompting arm, so read the abstract and table together.
agent_relevance: Quantifies why the model should not grade its own plan; once a real correct/incorrect signal exists, extra detail adds little.

source: Paglieri et al. (2025) BALROG: Benchmarking Agentic LLM and VLM Reasoning On Games
finding: Long-horizon partially observable games (BabyAI, Crafter, TextWorld, Baba Is AI, MiniHack, NetHack) for LLM agents.
numbers: Language-only average progress: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 32.64+/-1.93, GPT-4o 32.34+/-1.49, Llama 3.1 70B 27.88, Gemini 1.5 Pro 21.00, GPT-4o-mini 17.36, Llama 3.1 8B 15.14. NetHack best (o1-preview) 1.5% progress. Adding images lowered GPT-4o to 22.56.
limits: One prompt format per model; scores aggregate games of very different difficulty.
agent_relevance: Shows the practical gap on real POMDPs: models know facts (do not eat rotten food) but fail to apply them across many steps under partial observation.

source: Wang et al. (2025) RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn RL (StarPO)
finding: Trains LLM agents with trajectory-level RL on Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake (stochastic), WebShop. Finds the Echo Trap: reward variance collapses, entropy drops, gradients spike.
numbers: Collapse seen in Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake with GRPO and PPO; PPO more stable than GRPO; WebShop starts high and improves fast. StarPO-S filters trajectories by reward variance. Without reasoning-aware rewards, thoughts become shallow or hallucinated.
limits: Small models, stylised environments; no single headline accuracy extracted.
agent_relevance: Multi-turn RL on POMDP-like tasks: reasoning text can decorate rather than drive action. Supports not trusting written reasoning as a record of the decision (SCHEMA section 1).

source: Kaelbling, Littman & Cassandra (1998) Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
finding: Founding POMDP paper named in our row: the belief state is a sufficient statistic of history, and the optimal value function over beliefs is piecewise linear and convex (from background knowledge, not read this session).
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Gives the theory for why the program should hold the belief: a Bayes-updated distribution is all that is needed from the history.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2022) PlanBench
finding: Listed only as the source benchmark reused in the LLM-Modulo paper.
numbers: Figures come from the LLM-Modulo paper (line c13), not PlanBench itself.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Benchmark to run if we test the scaffold on classical planning.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) On the Planning Abilities of LLMs
finding: Origin of the 'GPT-3 plan success 1% vs humans 78%' blocks figure quoted in the RAP paper.
numbers: 1% vs 78% (second-hand, quoted inside RAP, line c01).
limits: Not opened directly.
agent_relevance: Shows the size of the gap that RAP-style search tried to close.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Listed as the heuristic-search baseline that RAP and UoT compare against.
numbers: UoT paper reports it beats adapted ToT by 12.4% success (line c11); no ToT numbers read directly.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: ToT lacks a stored state and a principled value; RAP and UoT add them.

source: Chen et al. (2021) Decision Transformer
finding: Listed as precursor: RL as sequence modelling, which DPT extends to in-context learning.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Background only.

source: Synthesis: sufficient statistic held by code (Krishnamurthy 2024; Nie 2024)
finding: Two independent bandit studies agree that giving the LLM a summary (per-arm means and counts) instead of raw history is the largest single lever for exploration.
numbers: Krishnamurthy: 1 working configuration, which requires the summary. Nie: summarised history 50.2% vs raw history 27.5% win-rate.
limits: Both are bandits with no transitions; in a real POMDP the belief is large and the summary design is unsolved.
agent_relevance: Design rule: the program keeps the belief (hypotheses with weights) and prints it each step.

source: Synthesis: explicit belief plus expected information gain (GATE 2023; OPEN 2024; UoT 2024)
finding: Three studies move from plain 'ask a question' (GATE) to explicit belief with information gain (OPEN, UoT); UoT's +38.1% success and OPEN's win over LM-only suggest the formal step helps.
numbers: UoT +38.1% average; OPEN beats LM-only pairwise in a user study.
limits: Different domains and metrics; not a controlled comparison.
agent_relevance: Candidate operator: with many hypotheses, pick the check or question that splits the weighted mass most evenly; code does the scoring.

source: Synthesis: sound verifier beats self-judgment (Valmeekam 2023; Kambhampati 2024; RAP ablation)
finding: Self-critique 55% vs sound verifier 88% on Blocksworld; RAP's self-evaluation reward degraded with more iterations; LLM-Modulo reaches 82% only with an external verifier.
limits: Blocksworld has clean rules; many real tasks lack a sound verifier.
agent_relevance: Reinforces G2 and G3. Where no sound checker exists, fall back on held-out or mutated checks.

source: Synthesis: boundary conditions of MDP search (RAP; LLM-MCTS; LLM-Modulo)
finding: Search helps most on novel and compositional tasks, fails when the LLM cannot propose plausible actions (Mystery Blocksworld about 10% even with a verifier), and costs far more compute.
numbers: LLM-MCTS compositional unseen 71.9 vs 43.3 policy-only; UCT without LLM prior 0.0.
limits: Costs not compared on equal token budgets in the sources I read.
agent_relevance: Use lookahead only when stakes and branching justify the cost; cap depth at 3 as UoT did.

source: Synthesis: written reasoning versus acting (RAGEN; BALROG)
finding: Models can state the right rule yet break it in action (BALROG NetHack), and RL can yield thoughts that do not drive actions (RAGEN).
numbers: BALROG NetHack best 1.5% progress; RAGEN Echo Trap collapse in 3 of 4 environments.
limits: Descriptive; no causal test.
agent_relevance: Hold decisions in code transitions; do not let model text decide.

source: Synthesis: models do not update beliefs like Bayes filters (Qiu 2025; Krishnamurthy 2024)
finding: Both studies show in-context updating plateaus or collapses into a greedy loop without help; training (Bayesian teaching) or an external summary repairs it.
numbers: Qiu: plateau after round 1 for most models; Krishnamurthy: suffix failures over 60% at T=500.
limits: Different tasks.
agent_relevance: Run the posterior update in code; give the model the updated numbers and ask only for the next hypothesis or action.

source: Synthesis: gap, no full-POMDP benchmark found
finding: I found no study in this session that measures a chat LLM on a classic POMDP (tiger, RockSample) against the optimal belief-MDP policy. The arXiv listing API, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were all rate limited, so search was by recalled IDs only.
numbers: None.
limits: Search coverage is partial; absence is not evidence of absence.
agent_relevance: Treat 'LLM on classic POMDP benchmarks' as a gap and a cheap test we could run ourselves.
